correctness.rationale: The hub coordinate exposes the two layers separately. Their crosspolytope and simplex span orthogonal direction spaces of dimensions m and m−1, and the centroid contrast has squared length 4+2/m; this gives intrinsic dimension 2m and all 3m genuine vertices. The proposed positive orbit masses α=(m+1)/(2m+1) and β=m/(2m+1) give mean c=h+βδ. Direct within-layer second moments give covariance eigenvalues 2α/m and 2β/m on the within-layer spaces and αβ||δ||² on the contrast. For Q=2m times this covariance, the layer gauges are (1+β/m)/(2α) and (m−1+α)/(2mβ), both exactly one; the latter also works when the simplex is a point. Weighted containment and trace–determinant AM–GM prove unrestricted optimality and uniqueness; strict convexity excludes nonvertex contacts. The common squared vertex norm and weighted mean prove the radius formula and ball optimality. Multiplying the eigenvalues with their multiplicities yields the exact ratio, and the logarithm of the ratio base differs from log(2/3) by 1/(6m)+O(m^−2). Independent m=1 and m=2 checks give, respectively, two equal squared axes 8/3 and squared axes 24/5, 8/5, 12/5, 12/5 with ratio 24sqrt(3)/49.
residual_risks: Scope is the canonical unweighted orthonormal-coordinate realization; no affine-metric or arbitrary-tree extension is inferred.

evidence: Write the centered star as conv[(A,0,−βL),(0,B,αL)], where A and B are the centered crosspolytope and simplex, L=||δ|| and the last coordinate is a unit contrast. Its polar is specified by h_A(p)≤1+βLt and h_B(q)≤1−αLt, with h denoting support. Its slices therefore exhibit the polar as the free join of A°/α at t=1/(αL) and B°/β at t=−1/(βL). The barycentric weights of zero are (α,β), exactly the theorem's weights for dimensions m and m−1.

The factors' polar John squared radii are 1/(2α²) and 1/(β²·2(m−1)/m), by symmetry of the crosspolytope and regular simplex and their circumradii. Multiplying by d_i τ_i/d gives the tangential squares of the polar join's John ellipsoid. The contrast interval has length 1/(αβL), so barycentric variance αβ/d gives contrast square 1/(dαβL²). Reciprocating yields 4α, 4β and dαβL², respectively, the frozen squared axes.

A John ellipsoid of the polar centered at the origin has a polarity-dual Löwner ellipsoid globally, not just among centered competitors: in unit-ball coordinates the John contact vectors are also in the primal body, since their polar supporting hyperplanes are tangent to the unit ball. The same zero first moment and identity second moment certify unrestricted outer optimality. Substituting the layer vertices into the reciprocal shape shows every generator touches; strict convexity excludes other contacts. The established ball radius and determinant then give the exact ratio and its elementary expansion.
